newsitem.title: UK: UK longer leading index falls for 10th month-NTC.
newsitem.headline: UK longer leading index falls for 10th month-NTC.

text.p: Britain's longer leading indicator, designed to indicate turning points in the business cycle about 13 months in advance, fell for the 10th month in a row in June, NTC Research said on Friday.

The index dropped to 89.1 in June from 90.9 in May and suggests a downturn from November this year. "History suggests that three consecutive monthly falls in the index signals a turning point in activity," NTC said.
It said downward pressure on the index had come mainly from rising short-term interest rates. Base rates have been jacked up to seven percent in four, quarter-point moves in as many months.
"A decline in business optimism and weaker growth in private housing starts contributed further to the index fall in June," NTC said.

The shorter leading index, which signals turning points in the economy about six months ahead, rose to 95.4 from 95.1. "Buoyant consumer confidence was once more the principal cause of the upturn," NTC said.
The coincident index dropped to 104.3 in June, from 104.9. It generally moves in line with the business cycle. -- Mike Peacock, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7708
